For example, financial services firms use decision support systems to assist with loan and mortgage payouts, wealth and asset management, investment and retirement planning, financial consultation, and credit risk assessment. The task of these decision support systems is often to estimate the model parameters and use them to suggest the best option. Hence, the consequences of the output of these engines, in areas such as loan rejection or mortgage denial, can often have a large impact.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.70593/978-93-49910-91-1_9\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 6, 10]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.4018/979-8-2600-2870-4.ch007\", \"title\": [\"Determining Responsibility for Artificial Intelligence-Based Security Decision Making\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The chapter discusses the determination of who is responsible when artificial intelligence is used for security decision making within complex organizational environments.
